newsitem.title: USA: Viad sells tower to Singapore group.
newsitem.headline: Viad sells tower to Singapore group.

text.p: Viad Corp. said Monday it has sold the Viad Tower here to a U.S. subsidiary of the Goverment of Singapore Investment Corp., a corporation owned by the Singapore government, for $73 million.
Completed in 1991, the 24-story building has about 484,000 square feet of rentable space and is located on the corner of Central Avenue and Palm Lane in the arts district of downtown Phoenix, Ariz.
Viad Realty Corp. has retained ownership of about one acre of land on the north side of the building that is zoned and permitted as a future site for a second tower.
"The sale of the tower is part of our continuing efforts to divest our non-core assets," said Robert Bohannon, president and chief executive of Viad.
Viad also said that it would lease back the space it occupies in the tower as part of the transaction.
Viad recently sold Premier Cruise Lines, Greyhound Lines of Canada, several bus terminals and a corporate jet, as well as its interest in the Phoenix Suns.
GSIC invests in large-scale commercial properties in North America, Europe and Asia. Viad's stock fell 25 cents to $16.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
